not_judged.TMR-ADDR-WIDTH-RANGE: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) always sets ADDR_WIDTH, to 4 and to 8 (lines 75, 1120 and 1121), so the default is never used and widths 5 to 7 are never built; a block whose default is 5, or that aliases offsets from 0x10 up only at width 6, passes it.
not_judged.TMR-PORTS-ONLY: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) connects the ports by name (lines 75 to 83), and Icarus Verilog builds an instance that leaves a port of the block unconnected, so a block with an extra port passes it. The widths of the named ports are checked (lines 461 to 480, TMR-PORTS).
not_judged.TMR-COUNT-READ: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) never checks the value of COUNT while a count runs: it compares COUNT with a value only at reset, after a one-shot count ends, after a COUNT write and after a stop (lines 314, 298, 331, 403 to 404, 409, 457, 529, 575, 577, 579 and 587). The two reads of a running COUNT (lines 428 and 430) check only that RDATA and RRESP hold still while RVALID waits and that the response is OKAY. The coverage matrix (lines 645 to 1113) likewise compares COUNT only with the count stopped: in its write sweep, where no count runs (line 798), after a one-shot count ends, and after a stop (lines 913, 958 and 1020). COUNT's value during a count is judged only through the edge the count ends on (TMR-COUNT, TMR-COUNT-LENGTH) and the value a stop leaves (TMR-STOP-EDGE).
not_judged.TMR-CTRL-WINS: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) never lands a CTRL write on the edge a count ends: its only writes timed to a count end are the STATUS clears at lines 395 to 398 and 441 to 444, and the stops of its periodic runs are checked to land before the next count end (lines 602 and 617). In the coverage matrix (lines 645 to 1113), the STATUS clears of each traced count land on count ends by design (lines 970 to 1023, TMR-END-BEATS-CLEAR), the stops of its periodic counts are checked to land before the next count end (lines 957 and 1019), a periodic count of LOAD 0 to 2, where every edge or every other one ends a count, is ended by a reset with no transfer in progress instead of a stop (line 1007), and its CTRL write matrix runs with LOAD 0x0010_0000, which never ends inside it. No mutant breaks this rule.
not_judged.TMR-READ-VALUE: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) never checks a value read on an edge on which that register changes: COUNT only while it holds still (see TMR-COUNT-READ; the reads of a running COUNT at lines 428 and 430 check no value), CTRL and STATUS only on edges on which no count ends, LOAD never during a write. So a read that returns the value after the accepting edge is not caught. The coverage matrix (lines 645 to 1113) keeps to the same: its overlapped reads (lines 1029 to 1060) read CTRL or an unmapped address while LOAD or an unmapped address is written.
not_judged.TMR-RESET-EDGE: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) drives aresetn low only at power up, where BVALID, RVALID and the held halves start unknown rather than high, and in the middle of a count with no transfer in progress (lines 274 to 282, 308 to 310 and 450 to 454), and in the coverage matrix between transfers, at its start and to end a periodic count of LOAD 0 to 2 (lines 1092 and 1007), changing it only between rising edges. So it never sees a pending response or a held half write dropped by reset, and does not tell a synchronous reset from an asynchronous one. The manager rule is an assumption on the testbench, which keeps it.
not_judged.TMR-CLEAN: Lint and synthesis are the RTL stage's own before-review checks, not held-out checks.
not_judged.TMR-TB-ALL: The must-fail check holds the flow's testbench to passing on the reference RTL and failing the four committed timer mutants (cited under mutants), and to nothing more: a testbench that leaves any other requirement of sections 2 to 6 unchecked, or times only some counts to the edge, still passes it.
not_judged.TMR-RESPONSE-EDGE-READY-HIGH: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) never has READY high on the edge a transfer completes: write() sets BREADY from b_seen_cyc, which is set only after BVALID is seen (line 130), and read() sets RREADY likewise (line 181); nothing else drives either (lines 51, 58, 159 and 208), and the coverage matrix reuses both tasks (lines 645 to 1113). So BVALID and RVALID are never watched rising with READY already high, and a block that drops a response when its READY is already high (bvalid <= !bready, rvalid <= !rready) passes it. TMR-RESPONSE-EDGE is judged only with READY low.
not_judged.TMR-READY-HELD-REQUEST: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) judges the values of AWREADY, WREADY and ARREADY on every edge (monitor, lines 703 to 707, TMR-READY) but never offers a request of a direction while a response of that direction waits: write() offers AWVALID and WVALID only until its own halves are accepted (lines 125 to 128) and returns after the response is taken (lines 148 and 157 to 158), and read() offers ARVALID likewise (lines 179 and 198 to 207); the overlap (lines 1029 to 1060) offers a read while a write response waits, and the reverse, which READY allows. So a block that accepts a new address or data on VALID alone while a response waits, with READY still low, passes it.
not_judged.TMR-RESPONSE-RDATA-STABLE: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) holds RDATA still while RVALID waits only for a read of a running COUNT (reads with RREADY late at lines 428 and 430, checked at line 193, TMR-RESPONSE), the one register that changes while a read of it waits. It never changes CTRL, LOAD or STATUS while a read of that register waits, so a block whose RDATA follows the live CTRL, LOAD or STATUS register while RVALID waits passes it.
not_judged.TMR-RUNNING-UNDISTURBED: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) lands only some transfers on a running count and then checks the count's end or its value: CTRL writes and CTRL reads (mx_ctrl, lines 872 to 919), LOAD writes (mx_load_mid, lines 923 to 960), STATUS clears (mx_count, lines 970 to 1020, and lines 395 to 398 and 441 to 444). The two reads of a running COUNT (lines 428 and 430) are followed by a stop, not by a count end or a COUNT value, and reads of LOAD, STATUS and unmapped addresses, COUNT writes and unmapped writes are never landed on a running count that is then checked (mx_unmapped, lines 776 to 800, runs with the count stopped). So a block where a read of COUNT, LOAD, STATUS or an unmapped address restarts or stalls the count, or where a COUNT write, an unmapped write or a STATUS write that clears nothing stalls, restarts or stops it, passes it.
not_judged.TMR-RESTART-MODE: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) restarts a running count only with the MODE it was started with (lines 411 to 419, and mx_ctrl in the coverage matrix, lines 872 to 919, where a restart does change MODE but LOAD is BIG, line 661, so no count ends and the MODE the restarted count ends under is never seen). So a block that latches MODE when the count starts and keeps it through a restart that writes the other MODE passes it.
not_judged.TMR-PERIODIC-EXPIRED-SET: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) clears EXPIRED after each end of a periodic count of LOAD above 2 or stops the count before the next end (lines 382 to 388, 395 to 402, 590 to 597, 605 to 617 and, in the coverage matrix, 940 to 957 and 1001 to 1019); with LOAD 1 and 2 EXPIRED stays set, but the count is ended by a reset (line 1007). So a block that does not reload a periodic count whose EXPIRED is already set, when LOAD is above 2, passes it.
not_judged.TMR-COUNT-32BIT: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) never lets COUNT borrow past bit 20 or end a count with a high bit set: its longest counts are 65539 and 0x0001_0005 cycles (lines 553 to 560, 1103 and 1108), mx_ctrl's BIG is 0x0010_0000 and its counts are stopped after a few edges (lines 661 and 872 to 919), and the stop from 0xFFFF_FFFF lasts 40 edges (lines 567 to 575), where only the low bits change. So a block that decrements only the low 24 or 28 bits, one that decides the count end on the low 21 to 31 bits, and one that reloads a periodic count with the low 24 bits of LOAD (a periodic count of LOAD above 0x0001_0005 never ends in a run) pass it.
not_judged.TMR-LOAD-END-EDGE: The document is silent on it (the clause states the open choice, and TMR-TEST-RANGE accepts both), and the reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) never lands a LOAD write on the edge a periodic count ends: mx_load_mid writes LOAD 4 to 6 cycles after the start of a count of 60 (lines 936 to 939) and nothing else writes LOAD during a count. A block that reloads the value written on that edge passes it, as does one that reloads the value held before it.

judged_scope.TMR-IRQ: Judged for 100000 cycles: the reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) holds irq high through 100000 idle cycles and through writes that do neither clear EXPIRED nor write IE 0 (lines 535 to 544, also line 8), and through the traced counts of the coverage matrix; a block whose irq ages out after more cycles than that (for example after 2^17) passes it.
